plans.note: Primary text in Section 21 (Limitation of Liability). Check mutuality of the cap, the multiplier/fee-measurement period, exclusion of indirect damages, and the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Section 1 as it likely drives the carve-outs; cross-check Section 20 indemnities are outside the cap.

Section 20 is the indemnification clause; verify Vendor IP infringement indemnity plus misconduct/data breach coverage, defence and control mechanics, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow. Section 14 may contain IP-specific remedies (modify/replace/refund) and Section 21 may cap the indemnity.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline. Scan Customer Responsibilities, Agreement Structure and General for any restriction on competing products, in-house builds, or use of alternative providers before concluding absent.

Look for sole-source or exclusive-provider language in Agreement Structure and Scope, Order Forms/Affiliate Orders, and Customer Responsibilities; exclusivity is sometimes buried in fee or order-commitment text in Section 7.

Check pricing terms in Section 7 and order mechanics in Section 4 for any best-terms/most-favoured pricing language. Only flag if the MFN runs against us; an MFN in our favour is welcome and should not be redlined.

Non-solicits typically sit in General (Section 30) or alongside personnel/confidentiality provisions. Test scope (employees involved in the Services only), duration (12 months preferred), mutuality, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Section 9 (Termination) is the primary locus; confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on notice without early-termination or penalty fees, and that any Vendor convenience right is absent or effective only at end of term. Section 10 may impose wind-down charges.

Section 8 (Term and Renewal) governs auto-renewal length and the non-renewal notice window; check any renewal price-uplift cap in Section 8 or Section 7. A missing uplift cap alone is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Section 28 covers governing law, venue and any arbitration or escalation steps. Vendor is a UK entity, so watch for English law plus foreign-seated arbitration; England and Wales law with courts is acceptable, offshore arbitration is not.

Section 24 addresses assignment and change of control. Confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that the Vendor has no termination right triggered by our change of control; check Section 30 for any residual boilerplate.

Section 14 governs ownership of Deliverables and Vendor Technology; Section 15 governs Customer Data ownership and any feedback/aggregated-data or improvement licences back to the Vendor. Check the Section 1 definitions of Deliverable, Customer Data and Vendor Technology for scope creep.

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence) is the grant clause; test that it extends to our Affiliates and contractors/users, is non-revocable during the term, and is not limited by suspension rights. Section 4 affiliate-order mechanics may supply affiliate coverage.

Section 22 is the audit right; confirm frequency (no more than annual), advance written notice, business-hours and remote/off-site preference, Vendor bears cost absent material underpayment, and confidentiality of auditors. Section 23 records obligations feed the same term — do not double-flag.

Check Section 7 for late-payment interest or penalty charges and Section 9/10 for early-termination fees payable by us. Service credits running to us under Section 3 are beneficial and should not be flagged.

Section 19 holds the warranties; test the performance/conformity warranty period, whether the remedy is re-performance plus refund, and whether disclaimers gut the warranty. Section 6 (Acceptance) and Section 3 service levels may supply the remedy mechanics.

Section 18 is a dedicated insurance clause; verify coverage lines (commercial general liability, professional/E&O, cyber), limits, and that certificates are available on request. Section 17 security obligations may reference cyber cover.

Look for committed spend, minimum volumes, non-reducible seat counts or true-up mechanics in Section 7 fees and Section 4 order forms; any take-or-pay must pair with a convenience exit under Section 9.

Section 11 is a dedicated transition assistance and data return clause; confirm the assistance period, that it applies on termination for any reason (including Vendor termination for our breach), the export format for Customer Data, and deletion/certification. Section 10 may condition assistance on payment.
